lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: one no or infinitely many solutions
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: one no or infinitely many solutions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: Classify the system: y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x - 1. Does it have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions?

steps: Both equations have the same slope, 2, so the lines are parallel.
The y-intercepts are different (3 and -1), so the lines never meet.
A system of parallel, non-identical lines has no solution.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: The reference equation is y = -6x - 17. Which of these equations, paired with the reference, would give the system infinitely many solutions?
Plan A charges a $9 flat fee plus $6 per week. Plan B charges a $17 flat fee plus $2 per week. After how many weeks do the two plans cost the same, and what is that cost?
Plan A charges a $47 flat fee plus $4 per visit. Plan B charges a $53 flat fee plus $2 per visit. The solution to the system is (3, 59). What does this solution represent?
choices: Plan A costs $59 more than Plan B after 3 visits.

items.prompt: System: y = -5x + 83 and y = 6x - 93. Does the point (17, 9) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?
Plan A charges a $110 flat fee plus $8 per month. Plan B charges a $35 flat fee plus $13 per month. The solution to the system is (15, 230). What does the x-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The flat fee charged by Plan A.
The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.
The number of months after which the two plans cost the same.
The difference in cost between the two plans.

items.prompt: System: y = -3x + 33 and y = -8x + 83. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?
Solve the system: y = 8x + 20 and y = -9x - 31. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
Relationship A: x: -6, -5, -4, -3 y: -7, -5, -3, -1. Relationship B: x: -6, -5, -4, -3 y: -7, -1, 5, 11. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?

Solve the system:
y = 5x - 13
7x - 3y = 7
